summary: Single-page web app for SOX Protocol — visual companion to the TUI demo. Consumes @sox-protocol/client (the only client dependency) and exercises the primitives that benefit most from a graphical surface: visible per-channel seq numbers in MessageThread, channel taxonomy distinguishing group/, dm/, and sox/ prefixes in ChannelSidebar, dm/<sorted-pair> rendering in a DM view, and a replay scrubber feature flag. Distributed two ways: standalone static deployment and a `sox ui` CLI subcommand that bundles assets into the Python wheel and serves them via the HTTP transport on a free local port.

stack.framework: React 18 + Vite — chosen over Next.js because the app is a static SPA bundled into a Python wheel (no SSR, no server-side routing); Vite gives fast HMR and a tiny production bundle that fits the 250KB gzipped budget
stack.state: Zustand — chosen over Jotai/TanStack Query because: (1) the SDK already provides AsyncIterable streams via watch(), so server-state caching is unnecessary; (2) Zustand's middleware composes cleanly with the SDK's drain helper; (3) lowest bundle cost (~1KB) of the three candidates
stack.styling: Tailwind CSS (JIT) — chosen for zero runtime cost, predictable bundle size via purge, and good a11y defaults via @tailwindcss/forms

deployment.static: Cloudflare Pages — chosen for free SSL, global edge cache, and Pages-native preview deployments per PR; the static bundle is also re-shipped inside the Python wheel for offline `sox ui` use
deployment.rationale: Two-pronged distribution: (1) public hosted demo at sox-protocol.dev/ui pointing at a public read-only namespace; (2) `pip install sox-protocol[ui]` bundles the same artifacts under packages/python/src/sox_protocol/ui_assets/ so `sox ui` works air-gapped

component_tree.note: self-presence indicator + manual heartbeat trigger; auto-heartbeat every 10s via store middleware

groups channels into three sections — Groups (group/ prefix), DMs (dm/<sorted-pair> rendered as 'peer name'), System (sox/ prefix); free-form channels under a fourth Channels section. Resolves dm/<a>~<b> back to peer ID via dm helpers from SDK.

renders seq number on each message bubble (visible affordance — this is the demo vehicle for sequence-numbers); reply_to draws a thread-link to parent in-view; uses thread_depth=1 when ancestor not in current window. Live updates via SDK watch() — no polling.
subscribes to sox/presence via SDK watch(); renders online/busy/stale/offline badges; coalesced events only (no per-heartbeat flicker)
supports reply_to (set when user clicks Reply on a message); generates correlation_id; surfaces backpressure state from send response
FEATURE FLAG replay_mode — slider over 1..currentSeq; calls SDK replay(channel, since, limit) with pagination; THIS is the webapp's primary replay coverage
FEATURE FLAG graph_view — force-directed graph of agents and reply_to edges; uses delivered_to to draw wait-graph
wraps MessageThread with channel resolved via SDK canonicalDmName(self,peer); renders 'peer name' header instead of raw dm/<sorted-pair>

feature_flags.graph_view: force-directed agent/message graph using reply_to + delivered_to edges; off by default; URL param ?ff=graph_view
feature_flags.replay_mode: MessageThread history scrubber using replay operation with seq cursor; off by default; URL param ?ff=replay_mode — this is the webapp's primary replay primitive coverage

cli_subcommand.name: sox ui
cli_subcommand.behavior: pick a free local port, start HTTP transport (CORS allow-list = http://localhost:* + http://127.0.0.1:*), mount packages/python/src/sox_protocol/ui_assets/ at /ui/, open default browser to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ui/, accept --port, --namespace, --no-browser, --bind flags

test_cases: sox ui boots, browser hits /ui/, sends a message, sees own message back via watch with seq=1
DM round-trip between two browser sessions

risks.risk: CORS in dev when SDK is on a different port than the static dev server
risks.mitigation: HTTP transport advertises permissive CORS for http://localhost:* and http://127.0.0.1:* by default; document allow-list extension
credential lives in sessionStorage only; lib/credential.ts has lint rule + test asserting no window.localStorage write

risks.risk: EventSource cannot send Authorization header from browser
risks.mitigation: fall back to query-param token on the SSE endpoint; documented as localhost-only; use reverse proxy in production

risks.risk: Bundle size blow-out from GraphView's force-directed library
risks.mitigation: GraphView is dynamically imported behind feature flag; default bundle stays ≤250KB gzipped; ci asserts size
store middleware persists last-seen seq per channel; on watch reconnect, calls SDK replay(since=lastSeq) before resubscribing — same recovery pattern as reference-agent
configure vitest coverage to omit src/components/*.tsx jsx return statements; documented in vitest.config.ts; logic dirs (state/, hooks/, lib/) keep 100%
